landmarks.q: Which Bathhouse Row bathhouse now houses a brewery and distillery?

landmarks.text: EoA calls the Hale, built in 1892-93, the oldest surviving bathhouse; the Buckstaff (1912), Fordyce (1914-15) and Lamar (1923) came later.
landmarks.q: Which is the oldest surviving bathhouse on Hot Springs' Bathhouse Row?

landmarks.text: Thompson, Sanders & Ginocchio's late-1930s remodel changed the facade from neo-Classical revival to Mission Style in 1939-40.
landmarks.q: In what architectural style was the Hale Bathhouse facade remodeled in 1939–40?

landmarks.text: The pool was installed in 1931 to treat paralysis; the Maurice was the only bathhouse to employ a registered physical therapist.
landmarks.q: What was the Maurice Bathhouse's 1931 therapeutic pool built for?

landmarks.text: The Fordyce reopened as the visitor center on May 13, 1989.
landmarks.q: Which Bathhouse Row building houses Hot Springs National Park's visitor center and museum?

landmarks.text: Its chevron-mosaic dome is topped by a small copper cupola.
landmarks.q: Which Bathhouse Row bathhouse is crowned by a large tiled dome?

landmarks.text: Scalloped shells frame the sculpin, originally gold and now white.

landmarks.text: NPS: the final metamorphosis of Bathhouse Row was completed when the Lamar opened in 1923; it closed in 1985.
landmarks.q: Which bathhouse's 1923 opening completed Hot Springs' Bathhouse Row?

landmarks.text: Work began in the 1930s on the promenade behind the bathhouses, which was finally completed in the early 1960s.
landmarks.q: In what decade did construction begin on the Grand Promenade behind Bathhouse Row?

nature.text: Both families are real neighbors: the park's species list counts the eastern gray squirrel as present and the fox squirrel as probably present.
nature.source: NPS NPSpecies, Hot Springs National Park mammals

nature.text: Fox squirrels are the bigger cousins: about 1½–2 lb in Arkansas, while gray squirrels weigh just over a pound.
A squirrel's leaf nest sits about 40 feet up, is 12–20 inches across, and can be built in under 12 hours.
Gray squirrels bury nuts one at a time and never find them all, so they plant new trees every fall.
Oak and hickory nuts in the region fall in September and October. Red-oak acorns take two years to ripen; white oak acorns take one.
nature.source: Missouri Department of Conservation tree guide

nature.text: Squirrels snip shortleaf pine cones and eat the seeds before the cones even open.
nature.source: USDA Forest Service, Silvics of North America

nature.text: Hedge apples (Osage-orange) are native to the Red River country of Oklahoma, Texas and Arkansas. Squirrels tear them open for the seeds.
Sweetgum "gumballs" aren't nuts: they are spiky 1–1½ inch seed balls that ripen in fall and hang on all winter.
The Ozark chinquapin still grows in the park but is rare: chestnut blight reached it by 1940, and volunteers now breed blight-resistant trees.
In fall, hickories turn golden yellow and sweetgums go red, orange, maroon and purple.
Redbuds bloom pink to reddish purple from March before their leaves come out; flowering dogwood follows with white bracts.
nature.source: USDA Forest Service, Silvics of North America

nature.text: Hot Springs breezes are gentle: at Memorial Field the wind averages about 5 mph and blows from the east more than any other direction (2016–2025 records).
